answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every new identity must plant a juniper stake: a refundable deposit locked in escrow before it can trade, released only after a season of verified work. Each completed task earns a signed receipt chained to the last, and randomly assigned peers audit the chain, so one forged receipt burns the deposit. A zephyr of cheap fake accounts cannot pass, because each must pay the same stake and do the same real work; buying ten thousand identities costs ten thousand deposits, and one forgery voids the opal-bright record they built.
